summary: The PR claims to be documentation-only, adding an Installation section to the README, but the diff contains no README changes at all. Instead it modifies index.js (reordering and rewriting the contraction/possessive regex) and adds a test case — directly contradicting the 'no code or behavior changes' claim.

statedClaims.text: Adds an Installation section to the README covering npm install slugify and yarn add slugify
statedClaims.explanation: No README file is touched anywhere in the diff. The only changed files are index.js and test.js. The core stated deliverable is entirely absent.

index.js changes the contraction/possessive handling: the regex is rewritten from matching '-t'/'-s' to matching apostrophes ('t/'s) and is moved to run before the main patternSlug replacement. This is a real behavior change, directly contradicting the claim.

inferredClaims.text: Slugify performs contraction/possessive replacement before applying the main character pattern replacement.
inferredClaims.explanation: The apostrophe-handling replace is moved above the `string.replace(patternSlug, options.separator)` line, so it now runs before the main pattern step.

inferredClaims.text: Strings containing possessives or contractions produce a slug where apostrophe characters are resolved correctly rather than stripped or mishandled.
inferredClaims.explanation: The new regex `/([a-zA-Z\d]+)'([ts])(\s|$)/g` operates on the raw apostrophe before slugification, matching the existing possessive tests (Conway's -> conways, etc.).

inferredClaims.text: The reordering does not alter slug output for inputs that contain no contractions or possessives.
inferredClaims.explanation: The added test guards one dashed-input edge case, but there is no broad verification that reordering leaves all non-contraction inputs unchanged; only reasoning supports it.

inferredClaims.text: Inputs with multiple apostrophes or mixed contractions and special characters are handled consistently under the new ordering.
inferredClaims.explanation: No new test covers multiple apostrophes or mixed special-character inputs under the new ordering.

inferredClaims.text: A test case is added covering the contraction/possessive replacement behavior.
inferredClaims.explanation: A test line is added, but it asserts a dashed input `it-s-hould-not-modify-t-his` is left unmodified — a negative/regression guard rather than a positive contraction/possessive case.

inferredClaims.text: The existing test suite continues to pass with the changed replacement ordering.
inferredClaims.explanation: Existing possessive/contraction assertions remain and appear consistent with the new regex, but the suite cannot be executed here to confirm.

inferredClaims.text: The added test demonstrates the corrected slug output for at least one contraction or possessive input.
inferredClaims.explanation: The single added assertion is not a contraction/possessive input; it checks that a dashed string is NOT modified, so it does not demonstrate corrected contraction/possessive output.

inferredClaims.text: Despite the PR title referencing README installation instructions, the actual change modifies index.js behavior; the mismatch should be reconciled.
inferredClaims.explanation: The mismatch is confirmed: no README change exists while index.js behavior and tests are modified, exactly the discrepancy this item flags.

unstatedChanges.description: Rewrites the contraction/possessive regex from dash-based ('-t'/'-s') to apostrophe-based (''t'/''s') and moves it to run before the main pattern replacement — a behavior change entirely unrelated to the stated documentation intent.
Adds a regression test asserting a dashed input is left unmodified, again unrelated to adding README installation instructions.
